assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, turned optical atomic spectroscopy into a measurement tool at the 10^-18 fractional-uncertainty level. This is the kind of new measurement capability that opens other science (relativistic geodesy, tests of constant variation, dark-matter searches, redefinition of the second). The underlying coherence, linewidth and systematic-control work is what I judge experiments by.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice trapping (2001-2003) and made the first demonstrations. Ye's group drove the strontium clock to the systematic-uncertainty frontier and the comb-clock link. Two laureates give a clean configuration. Ion-clock and frequency-comb work (already recognized in 2005 and 2012) is a separate matter, and I rely on my own recollection of the credit history rather than verification.
assessment.maturity: Heavily confirmed by many independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, and others) with repeated international clock comparisons. The interpretation is stable and the recognition is timely, with the redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views clocks as adequately distinct from the earlier 2005 and 2012 prizes for combs and ion control
Other contributors (for example Ye's JILA collaborators or Lemonde's early Sr work) could be argued for

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with laser-manipulated atoms provides absolute inertial sensors, gravimeters and gyroscopes, and measurements of G and the fine-structure constant. It is a clear case of a method that extends measurement precision and is moving into field instruments (geophysics, navigation), consistent with gravimetry uses I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Bordé gave the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer theory and early light-pulse ideas; Pritchard's group demonstrated atom interferometry with gratings and light, and Kasevich with Chu demonstrated the light-pulse gravimeter and precision measurements. Chu (a 1997 laureate for cooling) is not credited in this entry, so the credit boundary with his work is delicate, and I cannot resolve it from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and several mature instruments exist; sensitivity records continue to be set. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with Chu's earlier recognition and with Ramsey and Cohen-Tannoudji work
Distribution of credit among Bordé, Pritchard, Kasevich and Chu is disputed in the community

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realized Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters: the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics, and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This is a new way of observing many-body quantum physics, and a platform with wide influence on condensed-matter and quantum-simulation work.
assessment.attribution: The Mott transition demonstration (Greiner, Bloch and collaborators, 2002) and the fermionic Mott and band-structure experiments (Esslinger) are decisive experimental milestones; Zoller's theory (with Jaksch) provided the proposal and is a serious alternative to include. Quantum gas microscopes were developed by several groups, and I cannot settle the allocation among them.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, with a large and growing literature. Quantum simulators now address regimes beyond classical numerics, though the ultimate claim of useful simulation is still maturing.
uncertainties: Zoller's theory contribution versus the experimentalists, which is a real allocation question
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with candidates B015 and B035 involving Zoller
Whether the physics-discovery content is judged as a platform rather than a single discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Electromagnetically induced transparency and the slow and stopped light that follows from it are a clean coherent-control phenomenon. It underlies optical quantum memories, narrowband filters and nonlinear optics at the single-photon level. I know this physics at close range from spectral-hole and slow-light work in crystals.
assessment.attribution: Harris developed the theory and first demonstrations of EIT (with Field and Imamoglu in 1990-91); Hau's group demonstrated ultraslow light in a BEC (1999) and stopped light. Imamoglu's early theoretical contribution is credible, so the choice of two of three is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in vapors, cold atoms, and solids, with applications now in memories and metrology. It is mature and long-standing, and recognition could be seen as late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Dispute over priority between EIT, lasing without inversion and coherent population trapping (Alzetta, Arimondo, Gray)
Whether the effect is judged as a fundamental discovery or an enabling technique

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links the foundations of quantum mechanics with a practical cryptographic primitive, and has been taken from principle to fibre and satellite demonstrations. The conceptual originality is high and the technology has impact beyond physics.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84; Ekert independently proposed an entanglement-based protocol (1991) connected to Bell inequality tests. The three-name configuration is natural but the relative standing of BB84 and E91 is a matter of judgement.
assessment.maturity: Many experimental demonstrations exist, but practical security (side channels, device-independence, rates over distance) is not fully settled. The foundational concept is mature; deployed systems are less so.
uncertainties: Security of real implementations versus idealized protocols
Overlap with the 2022 prize on entangled-photon experiments and with Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea, which is not credited here

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond gave a room-temperature solid-state qubit with spin coherence times that support nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and biological sensing. It is a measurement technique with demonstrated reach into medicine and materials, though still partly at the laboratory scale.
assessment.attribution: Gruber, Wrachtrup and colleagues (1997) reported single-centre optical detection, and Jelezko and Wrachtrup then demonstrated coherent spin control (2004). Lukin and others made major contributions to sensing protocols and quantum registers; I limit my proposal to the earliest decisive demonstrations, and the allocation remains debatable.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by numerous groups and commercial instruments are emerging. Quantum-sensing advantage claims in applications (for example in vivo) are still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the single-centre detection and the sensing protocols should be credited together or separately
Contributions of Lukin, Awschalom, Hanson, Yacoby and others

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coherent interfaces between flying photons and stationary atomic ensembles or single atoms are the basis of quantum repeaters and memories. This is close to my own field, and I know how demanding the demonstrated efficiencies and storage times are in practice.
assessment.attribution: Kimble pioneered the quantum-network concept and cavity-QED experiments; Cirac and Zoller developed the theoretical architecture (quantum state transfer, repeater proposals with Briegel and Duan-Lukin). Credit is spread over many groups (Polzik, Lukin, Gisin, Kuzmich), which makes a three-person prize unclear.
assessment.maturity: Basic elements have been shown repeatedly, but fully functional networks with performance beyond fibre limits are not yet shown, so the field is only partly mature.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution across theory and several experimental groups
Whether recognition is premature given incomplete network demonstrations
Overlap with B015 and B008 on Cirac and Zoller

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed states of light improve interferometer sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit and are now operating in gravitational-wave detectors. This is a measurement improvement with concrete, demonstrated impact.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed squeezed-vacuum injection (1981) and Kimble's group produced early squeezed light (1985-86). Schnabel and the LIGO and GEO600 teams carried the technique to operating detectors; whether that engineering is a separate recognition is unclear. I propose only the origin pair.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is routinely used in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600 with independent confirmation. The concept is mature, though the Nobel recognition of LIGO in 2017 may be thought to have covered part of its impact.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2017 LIGO prize and 2012 and 2005 quantum-optics prizes
Credit for the experimental squeezing of Slusher, Wu and others is not in the credited list
Whether Schnabel's detector implementation should replace Kimble
